name: Anthropic
text:
We’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new wholly owned entity dedicated entirely to the public benefit.

It will start off with 5% of our shares. For every 50% increase in the company’s value over a set baseline, we can contribute up to an extra 2%, subject to our board’s discretion.

In total, this means that roughly 20% of Anthropic’s shares are committed to the public good. Our co-founders have already pledged to donate 80% of their equity, and around half our employees are donating a portion of their equity as part of a donation matching program we’ve run since our founding.

In the post below, we share more details about our new fund.

https://t.co/XzDntVH0vH
take: A big pledge with the rules still to come. Watch who decides how the money is spent before judging it.

name: OpenCode
text:
We had a security breach last night related to a large scale distillation attack that impacted 1.4% of OpenCode Console users

We have notified them all this morning via email. If you did not get an email you were not impacted, it was a subset of users who had external providers linked

The incident is ongoing so we cannot share more details at this point but we are working with Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google to remediate
take: If a tool stores your AI keys, it can run up your bill. Put a spending cap on every key today.

name: dax
text:
they've been non stop trying to attack our systems for the past 48 hours

take: Attackers now work around the clock with automation. Defenders without the same help fall behind.

name: DeepSeek
text:
🚀 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is here!

Stronger benchmark performance, faster task completion, and shorter outputs than the previous version—a Pareto improvement in performance and cost. Now live on our website, app, and API.

🛠️ Optimized for @DeepSeekHarness, Tencent CodeBuddy, WorkBuddy, and more. Upgrade to DeepSeek Harness v0.2.1-rc.1 or later for the best experience with the new model.

1/4
take: Another strong open model you can run yourself. Test it on your own tasks before trusting the benchmark chart.

name: Aravind Srinivas
text:
Users are reverse engineering and porting software across platforms with Perplexity Computer. This user's mechanical keyboard app was Windows only, with no Linux support and no documentation. Computer downloaded the binary in its cloud sandbox, decompiled it with headless Ghidra, and ported it to a native Rust app for Linux.

Computer read the decompiled code to learn how the app drives the keyboard, then rebuilt it piece by piece, complete with keyboard lighting that syncs to music over PipeWire, a 3D view, key remapping, macros and profiles.

https://t.co/eDZwppdI6c

https://t.co/OPmnDMqurt
take: Agents can now read decompiled code and move apps between platforms. Old software with no documentation is suddenly a migration project, not a dead end.

name: Greg Brockman
text:
6 days and $40,000 of compute with GPT-5.6 Sol to find a critical vulnerability in Chrome, claiming Google’s first full-chain reward in 2026 for a vulnerability that would affect an estimated 1 billion users.

Highlights the opportunity for defenders to utilize these tools to secure their software to unprecedented levels:
take: Finding serious bugs just got cheap. If you ship software, budget for AI-assisted security reviews now, before attackers do the same maths.

name: Demis Hassabis
text:
Gemini 4 Argon is amazing for knowledge work and coding - and it’s super fun to build with! We asked it to create this wizard chess game and it's so cool to see Argon's physics understanding & 3D modelling capabilities, makes me nostalgic for Battlechess on the Amiga - fun times!

Argon is rolling out today to Google Ultra and Pro subscribers in the @GeminiApp and Search, and Ultra subscribers in @antigravity! More info & full availability in the blog: https://t.co/7d3791mRNH
take: A new top-tier model you may already pay for. Try it on one real task from your week before you decide anything.

name: Aravind Srinivas
text:
Every Perplexity Project is a Git repo. We built a Git forge for agents, without the GitHub bloat, since no human has to approve anything.

Each agent gets its own short-lived sandbox and commits to a shared repo on S3. Fewer than 2% of submissions collide.

Agents search with plain `ls` and `grep`. That beats semantic search 63% vs 37% on answer accuracy for financial document analysis.
